## MacHub (https://machub.space/)

# MacHub

> MacHub is a free Mac app with 14 developer tools: device logs, APK/AAB/IPA analyzer, AAB to APK converter, payload decoder, diff, OCR, git clone and more. Local-first, no account. Anonymous usage stats are opt-in.

MacHub is a free macOS app (v1.1.0, macOS 12+, Apple Silicon and Intel). Distributed as a DMG from https://machub.space/download/.

## Tools

### Files & Paths

- **Path Checker**: Paste or drop a path and instantly see whether it is a file, a folder or missing. Reveal it in Finder, copy it, and revisit your last 50 checks.
- **File Utilities**: Bookmark the files you edit often, like ~/.zshrc or /etc/hosts, and open them in any app or run a saved shell command on them.
- **Dir Utilities**: Tag and filter your workspace folders, then open them in Finder, VS Code, Cursor, Android Studio, Xcode, IntelliJ, iTerm and more.

### Text & Data

- **Payload Decoder**: Auto-detects and unwraps layered payloads (JWT, JSON, URL encoding, hex, Gzip, Base64) up to eight layers deep, shown as a JSON tree.
- **Data Format**: Pretty-print or minify JSON, XML, HTML, YAML, CSV, query strings, SQL and CSS, with find and a tree view.
- **Text Diff**: Side-by-side diff with line and character-level highlights, next/previous navigation and search.
- **Base64 Image**: Decode one or many base64 strings or data URIs into images you can preview, repair, copy or save in bulk.

### Devices & Packages

- **Device Logs**: Live adb logcat, flutter logs and iOS syslog (devices and simulators) with level, package and text filters.
- **Package Analyzer**: Inspect any APK, AAB or IPA: versions, SDKs, permissions, signing, native libraries, provisioning and a size breakdown.
- **Project Analyzer**: Scan a folder for languages, lines of code, largest files and detected stacks, with a git change summary.
- **AAB to APK**: Convert an Android App Bundle into an installable universal APK with bundletool, then install it on a connected device.

### Utilities

- **Screenshot OCR**: Capture any region and read its text with Apple Vision, on your Mac. Optionally translate it into 15 languages.
- **Custom Commands**: Save the shell commands you keep retyping and run them in the background or in Terminal.
- **Git Clone**: Clone through the right SSH account alias and add web and upstream remotes in one go.

## Privacy

No account and no ads. Data stays in local preferences. Anonymous usage statistics are off unless you choose Share when MacHub asks, and you can change that in Settings › Privacy. Other network requests happen only when you ask: Google Translate (OCR translation), the GitHub API (fork parent lookup) and the Changelog page. See https://machub.space/privacy/.

## FAQ

### Is MacHub free?

Yes. MacHub is free to download and use.

### Does MacHub collect my data?

Only if you choose to share anonymous usage statistics. There is no account, no crash reporting and no ads. The first time you open MacHub it asks whether to share usage statistics; nothing is sent unless you choose Share, and you can change that anytime in Settings › Privacy. Your bookmarks, commands and history stay in your Mac’s local preferences. The other network requests the app can make only happen when you ask for them; see [the Privacy Policy](https://machub.space/privacy/).

### Which Macs does it run on?

macOS 12 Monterey or later, on Apple Silicon and Intel. Automatic language detection in Screenshot OCR for Chinese, Japanese and Korean needs macOS 13 or later.

### Why isn’t it on the Mac App Store?

MacHub launches tools such as adb, git and bundletool and reads files you choose, so it runs outside the App Sandbox. That is why it is distributed as a DMG from this site.

### Do I need the Android SDK, Flutter or git installed?

Only for the tools that use them. MacHub looks in the usual locations, shows an install hint when something is missing, and lets you point it at the right file with **Set path…**.

## Download MacHub for Mac (https://machub.space/download/)

# Download MacHub for Mac

> MacHub v1.1.0 for macOS 12+, Apple Silicon and Intel. Free.

One DMG for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. Free.

- **Version:** 1.1.0
- **Requires:** macOS 12 or later
- **Architecture:** Apple Silicon & Intel
- **Price:** Free

## Install

- Open `MacHub.dmg`.
- Drag **MacHub** into your **Applications** folder.
- Open MacHub from Applications or Launchpad.

## If macOS says MacHub can’t be opened

MacHub is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so macOS only asks you to confirm the first launch by clicking **Open**. If macOS still blocks it, do either of these once:

- Right-click (or Control-click) MacHub in Applications, choose **Open**, then **Open** again.
- Or open **System Settings › Privacy & Security**, scroll to the message about MacHub and click **Open Anyway**.

Only download MacHub from machub.space.

## Optional tools

MacHub works on its own. Some tools use command-line programs you install separately:

- **Device Logs:** `adb` (Android platform-tools), `flutter`, `idevicesyslog` (libimobiledevice) and Xcode’s `xcrun`
- **AAB to APK:** `bundletool` (`brew install bundletool`), plus Java if you use a `bundletool.jar`, and `adb` for installing
- **Git Clone and Project Analyzer:** `git`
- **Package Analyzer:** `apksigner` from the Android SDK build-tools is optional

## Permissions you may be asked for

- **Screen Recording:** Screenshot OCR captures a region you select
- **Automation:** opening Terminal for commands and a Finder fallback for protected files
- **Full Disk Access (optional):** only if you bookmark files macOS protects

## Uninstall

Quit MacHub and drag it to the Trash. To remove its saved data too, see [How do I reset MacHub?](https://machub.space/support/#reset)

## MacHub Support (https://machub.space/support/)

# MacHub Support

> Help, FAQ and contact for MacHub.

Find a quick answer below, or email us and include your macOS version and the tool you were using.

### Contact

Questions, bug reports and feature requests are welcome.

[Email support](mailto:machub1193@gmail.com)

### Download

Get the latest MacHub for macOS 12 or later.

[Download .dmg](https://machub.space/download/)

### Support MacHub

If MacHub saves you time, you can [buy me a coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/huynguyennovem).

### macOS says MacHub can’t be opened or is from an unidentified developer

MacHub is notarized by Apple, so macOS only asks you to confirm the first launch. If it still blocks the app, right-click MacHub in Applications and choose **Open**, or use **Open Anyway** in System Settings › Privacy & Security. See [the download page](https://machub.space/download/#gatekeeper).

### A tool says adb, flutter, bundletool, git or java was not found

MacHub checks common install locations (Homebrew, the Android SDK, your login shell) and remembers what it finds. If a tool is installed somewhere unusual, click **Set path…** in the banner and enter its full path. Homebrew users can run `brew install bundletool` or `brew install openjdk`.

### Screenshot OCR captures nothing or a blank image

Allow MacHub under **System Settings › Privacy & Security › Screen Recording**, then quit and reopen MacHub. Automatic language detection for Chinese, Japanese and Korean needs macOS 13 or later; macOS 12 reads Latin script only.

### MacHub can’t open one of my bookmarked files

macOS protects some locations. Grant MacHub **Full Disk Access** in System Settings › Privacy & Security, then try again.

### Convert & Install fails with INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE

The app on your device was signed with a different key than the one MacHub used. Uninstall the existing app from the device, or enable **Use custom keystore** and sign with the original key.

### The device list is empty in Device Logs or Convert & Install

Connect the device, enable USB debugging, accept the prompt on the device, then click the refresh button next to the device picker. Devices marked unauthorized or offline cannot be used until they are authorized.

### Which Macs are supported?

macOS 12 Monterey or later, on Apple Silicon and Intel.

### How do I reset MacHub?

Quit MacHub, then run `defaults delete com.app.machub` in Terminal. This removes bookmarks, saved commands, history, tool paths and preferences. To uninstall, also drag MacHub to the Trash.

To stop sharing anonymous usage statistics, turn off Settings › Privacy › Share anonymous usage data. To also remove the random identifier used for usage statistics, delete the `com.telemetrydeck.*.plist` files in `~/Library/Preferences` (this also resets other apps that use TelemetryDeck).

- **Base64 Image:** Decode one or many base64 strings or data URIs into images you can preview, repair, copy or save in bulk.
- **Device Logs:** Live adb logcat, flutter logs and iOS syslog (devices and simulators) with level, package and text filters.
- **Package Analyzer:** Inspect any APK, AAB or IPA: versions, SDKs, permissions, signing, native libraries, provisioning and a size breakdown.
- **Project Analyzer:** Scan a folder for languages, lines of code, largest files and detected stacks, with a git change summary.
- **AAB to APK:** Convert an Android App Bundle into an installable universal APK with bundletool, then install it on a connected device.
- **Screenshot OCR:** Capture any region and read its text with Apple Vision, on your Mac. Optionally translate it into 15 languages.
- **Custom Commands:** Save the shell commands you keep retyping and run them in the background or in Terminal.
- **Git Clone:** Clone through the right SSH account alias and add web and upstream remotes in one go.

## MacHub Privacy Policy (https://machub.space/privacy/)

# MacHub Privacy Policy

> No account, no ads, usage statistics are opt-in. Last updated October 17, 2026.

**Last updated:** October 17, 2026

This policy explains what the MacHub app and the machub.space website do with information. In short: the app has no account and no advertising, and it sends anonymous usage statistics only if you choose to share them.

## 1. Overview

MacHub is a desktop toolbox for macOS. It works with files, folders, text and command-line tools that you choose. The developer does not receive that content.

## 2. Data stored on your Mac

MacHub saves the following in your Mac’s local preferences (`~/Library/Preferences/com.app.machub.plist`):

- Bookmarked files and folders, tags, and the custom editor or command you attach to them
- Saved Custom Commands
- Last-used folders, tool paths, theme, sidebar and usage statistics settings
- History for Path Checker, Payload Decoder, Data Format and Text Diff (up to 50 entries each)

History entries can contain the full text you pasted, including tokens or other secrets. Delete the preferences to remove everything (see [How do I reset MacHub?](https://machub.space/support/#reset)).

MacHub also writes temporary files, for example the Screenshot OCR capture and images you copy from Base64 Image, to your Mac’s temporary folder. Files you export or save go where you choose.

## 3. Network requests

MacHub does not check for updates. The app makes a network request only when you use one of these features or turn on usage statistics:

- **Screenshot OCR › Translate:** sends the recognized text and the target language to Google Translate. Text recognition itself runs on your Mac.
- **Git Clone › upstream remote:** for github.com repositories, asks the GitHub API (unauthenticated) for the fork’s parent repository.
- **About › Changelog:** loads the changelog page in an in-app web view.
- **Usage statistics (optional):** if you choose Share, sends anonymous usage signals to TelemetryDeck (see section 8).

Those services handle data under their own privacy policies.

## 4. Tools you run

Git Clone, Device Logs, AAB to APK, Custom Commands and similar tools run programs such as `git`, `adb` and `bundletool` with your user permissions. Any network access by those programs, or by commands you write, is governed by the programs and services involved. MacHub reads host aliases from `~/.ssh/config` (not your keys) and checks for `~/.android/debug.keystore`.

## 5. Permissions

- **Screen Recording:** to capture the region you select for OCR, only when you start a capture
- **Automation (Apple Events):** to open Terminal for commands and as a Finder fallback
- **Full Disk Access:** optional, only for files macOS protects

## 6. Clipboard

MacHub reads the clipboard only when you press a Paste button. It writes to the clipboard when you press a Copy action. It never monitors the clipboard.

## 7. Keystore passwords

Passwords you enter for a custom keystore are not saved. They are passed to bundletool as command-line arguments while a conversion runs, so other processes on your Mac could briefly see them. They are masked in MacHub’s on-screen log.

## 8. Usage statistics, ads and accounts

The app contains no advertising or crash-reporting SDKs and requires no account.

**Usage statistics are optional.** The first time you open MacHub it asks whether to share anonymous usage statistics. Nothing is sent unless you choose Share, and you can change this anytime in Settings › Privacy.

If you share, MacHub sends signals to [TelemetryDeck](https://telemetrydeck.com/privacy), an analytics service that states it hosts data in the European Union and does not store IP addresses. A signal can contain:

- An anonymous identifier: a random ID created on your Mac, salted and hashed on your Mac, then hashed again by TelemetryDeck
- A session identifier and simple usage counters, such as the date of your first session and how many days and sessions you have used the app
- The app version and build, the day of the week and the hour
- Your Mac model, CPU architecture, macOS version, screen size, time zone, language and region
- Appearance and accessibility settings, such as light or dark mode and Reduce Motion
- The name of a tool when you open it, and a signal when you press the donate button

It never sends your files, paths, text, commands, logs, device serial numbers, package names, Git URLs or keystore data.

Turning sharing off stops sending. The random ID and the usage counters stay in a preferences file on your Mac (`~/Library/Preferences/com.telemetrydeck.*.plist`) until you delete it, and signals that could not be delivered yet are kept in your Mac's cache.

## 9. This website

machub.space is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages, which may log visitor IP addresses under GitHub’s privacy statement. The site sets no cookies and runs no analytics. Your light or dark theme choice is stored in your browser’s local storage.

The DMG is served through a Cloudflare Worker. To limit abuse it uses your IP address to count downloads (a small number per hour), and may ask you to complete a Cloudflare Turnstile check. Cloudflare processes that data under its own policies.

## 10. Children

MacHub is a developer tool and is not directed at children under 13.

## 11. Changes

We may update this policy. The date at the top shows the latest revision.

## 12. Contact

Questions: [machub1193@gmail.com](mailto:machub1193@gmail.com)

MacHub is a free desktop app for macOS that bundles developer utilities. Features may change over time.

## 3. Third-party tools and services

MacHub works with software it does not include, such as adb, Flutter, bundletool, Java and git, and can call services such as Google Translate and the GitHub API. Those are governed by their own licenses and terms.

## 4. Your responsibility

MacHub runs commands and reads or changes files on your Mac with your permissions, including commands you write yourself and installs onto connected devices. Review what you run, keep backups, and only use MacHub on files, devices and accounts you are authorized to use. Keep your keystores and passwords safe.

## 5. Downloads and updates

Download MacHub only from machub.space. We are not responsible for copies obtained elsewhere. Download limits may apply.
